parsed.explanation: A trans visitor presenting female is directly exposed under Section 379, a male-dress-as-woman offence carrying up to three months' imprisonment, with no documented moratorium or repeal. Same-sex conduct law carries up to 10-14 years but is reported unenforced 2018-2022 and is secondary. Security forces are nevertheless reported across 2018-2022 to harass, arrest, detain, torture and beat LGBTQI+ people, the 2017 minister threatened detention until procreation, a support group was raided and closed, and most openly LGBTQI+ citizens fled. No hate-crime or general anti-discrimination protection, no support organisations and no documented remedy exist. No documented Section 379 prosecution prevents a 0.15 rating; documented state abuse and an active appearance offence prevent a higher one.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Security forces reported to arrest, detain, beat and torture LGBTQI+ people 2018-2022; 2017 minister threatened detention until procreation.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: None documented; no recourse after detention reported.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Appearance under Section 379 can trigger the documented security-force pattern; custody placement for trans visitors is not documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Section 379 applies nationwide to public presentation in women's clothing; no subnational variation documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Nationwide dress exposure reaches every public facility and street encounter; specific bathroom or ward rules are not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Section 379 criminalises appearance alone; official rhetoric is hostile, minister ordered arrests in 2017, head of state rejected homosexuality in 2010.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No repeal or moratorium documented; same-sex conduct law remains on books though reported unenforced.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing plus security-force abuse makes the dress law an operative police lever, not merely a dead letter.

minors_guardians.interaction: No age-specific rule documented; any accompanying minor would face the same hostile state climate if the traveller is outed.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Security forces reported to harass, arrest, detain, torture and beat LGBTQI+ people; widespread stigma documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No hate-crime or general anti-discrimination law; only oil and gas employees as of 2020.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police are perpetrators, not protection; most openly LGBTQI+ citizens fled and no support organisations are known.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Support group raided in 2017, staff detained months without charge, organisation closed; NGO Act may bar LGBTQ groups.
remedies_unknowns.protection: No documented victim remedy or protection route.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absence of organisations and recourse converts documented abuse into unremedied exposure; Section 379 enforcement specifics remain unknown.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar direct appearance criminalisation and state abuse, but 0.15-A documents repeated convictions and custody sexual assault under sweeps; here no Section 379 prosecution is sourced, so this case sits slightly above 0.15.
Similar police raids, detention and extortion risk with failed complaints, but this dossier adds reported torture and a ministerial detention threat, placing it below the 0.25 profile on severity.
Much higher risk than 0.35-A: beyond an unremedied universal exclusion, there is an explicit appearance offence, documented security-force torture and no protective remedy.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is nationwide and hostile: Section 379 makes a trans woman's public presentation itself punishable, security forces are documented perpetrators of arrest, detention, beating and torture, and official rhetoric frames LGBTQI+ people as threats. The unenforced same-sex statute is secondary and does not dominate. The sectoral oil-and-gas employment protection does not reach visitors. With no entry, facility, care or custody information, and no functioning remedy, the documented exposures govern; the absence of sourced dress-law prosecutions keeps the rating above the severe 0.15 tier.
